title: Module quiz: Exploring a large codebase

questions.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. After a crash, one agent is started again from material it wrote out earlier. What should its new prompt hold?

options.text: Its assignment alone, because the saved material is implied by it
options.says: Ruled out because the prompt "carries its task, the state lines it exported", so the notes are not implied.

options.text: Its assignment and the complete old transcript, so that nothing is lost
options.says: Ruled out because "It does not get the old transcript, which is what filled the first window".

options.text: Its assignment, the exported notes and an instruction to continue
options.says: The page says the prompt "carries its task, the state lines it exported, and one instruction: continue from the first unfinished step".

options.text: The saved notes alone, because the assignment is contained in them
options.says: Ruled out because the prompt "carries its task, the state lines it exported", and the task comes first.

questions.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. A team needs a code-searching helper whose work can be picked up later in the same session. Which fits?

options.text: The built-in Explore subagent, continued with its own history
options.says: Ruled out because "The built-in Explore agent is one-shot".

options.text: A custom subagent, continued with its own history
options.says: A custom subagent can be resumed with its history, and the built-in one cannot.

options.text: A fresh Explore each time, handed a copy of the earlier transcript
options.says: Ruled out because "the transcripts are what filled the window".

options.text: A second coordinator that reads the first coordinator's conversation
options.says: Ruled out because "a crash that ended the session leaves only the files", and an ordinary session leaves a resumable subagent.

questions.stem: Scenario S4, developer productivity with Claude. A session finishes one exploration, and an unrelated piece of work then begins in the same window. Which step fits?

options.text: Turn compaction off for the new job so that no detail is lost
options.says: Ruled out because "Turning compaction off is not a remedy: the window then fills, and performance degrades".

options.text: Compact it with instructions to keep everything the first job found
options.says: Ruled out because "Compaction continues the same work with a shorter memory of it".

options.text: Enlarge the context limit so that both jobs fit side by side
options.says: Ruled out because "a bigger window only moves the problem later".

options.text: Clear the conversation, since nothing from the first job is needed
options.says: The page says "`/clear` starts over and is right between unrelated tasks".
